mainTopic: פתח פתוח: why a husband's claim is believed, ספק ספיקא, and reconciling רבי אלעזר's statements about what forbids a wife
overview: רבי אלעזר rules that a husband who says 'I found an open opening' (פתח פתוח), meaning his bride was not a בתולה, is believed to forbid her to himself. The גמרא asks why, since there is a ספק ספיקא: maybe it happened before the אירוסין, and even if after, maybe it was אונס. It answers that the case is an אשת כהן, who is forbidden even through אונס, or a girl betrothed before age three, so only one doubt remains. The גמרא then asks what the ruling adds, since a משנה already shows a man can forbid things to himself by his own word. It answers that here he might be mistaken, yet he is still believed. Next, the גמרא raises a contradiction from another statement of רבי אלעזר: a wife is forbidden only through קינוי וסתירה, as learned from the story of דוד and בת שבע. After clearing up that statement's wording, the גמרא rereads it as being about evidence. Two witnesses forbid a wife, after קינוי וסתירה one witness is enough, and פתח פתוח counts like two witnesses. Finally, it asks why בת שבע was not forbidden. It answers that it was אונס, and begins a second answer from רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The husband is believed to forbid his wife to himself
steps.stepSummary: A husband who claims he found his bride was not a בתולה is believed to make her forbidden to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a husband says, 'I found an open opening,' meaning his bride was not a בתולה, he is believed to make her forbidden to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a ruling of רבי אלעזר (his name appears just before this, at the end of the previous amud): a husband who claims his new wife was not a בתולה is believed, and she becomes forbidden to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His claim suggests she may have been with another man after the אירוסין, which would be זנות and forbid her to him. No witnesses are needed. His own word is enough to forbid her to himself.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'open opening': a claim that the bride was not a בתולה
Believed, trusted
To make her forbidden to himself

steps.confusionAlert: He is believed only to forbid her to HIMSELF. This step does not say she loses her כתובה or is punished.

phrases.english: One who says: 'I found an open opening'
phrases.notes: He means that when he was with his new wife, he found she was not a בתולה.

phrases.english: is believed to make her forbidden to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר פֶּתַח פָּתוּחַ מָצָאתִי נֶאֱמָן לְאוֹסְרָהּ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion with the base ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband claiming פתח פתוח is believed to forbid his wife to himself.

steps.title: Why forbid her if there is a double doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: there are two layers of doubt, and with a ספק ספיקא we usually rule leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why should she be forbidden? This is a double doubt. Maybe it happened after the אירוסין, maybe before. And even if it was after, maybe she was forced, maybe it was willing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from step 1. It points out two separate doubts that should allow her to stay permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doubt one: maybe it happened before the אירוסין, when she was not yet his, so she is not forbidden. Doubt two: even if it was after, maybe it was אונס (forced), which does not forbid an אשת ישראל. With two doubts both pointing toward permitted, the normal rule is to be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A double doubt; usually we rule leniently
'Under him': while she was already bound to him (after אירוסין)
Forced, against her will
Willingly

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole סוגיא. Every answer that follows must explain how one of these two doubts is removed.

phrases.english: But why?
It is a double doubt:
maybe it was under him, maybe it was not under him.
phrases.notes: 'Under him' means after the אירוסין, when she already belonged to him.

phrases.english: And if you say it was under him:
maybe by force, maybe willingly!

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the husband's claim forbids her to him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two independent doubts (before or after אירוסין; forced or willing) make a ספק ספיקא, which should lead to leniency.

steps.title: Answer: the case is the wife of a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is about an אשת כהן, who is forbidden even if forced, so only one doubt remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for the wife of a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by placing the ruling with the wife of a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשת כהן becomes forbidden to her husband even through אונס. So the 'forced or willing' doubt no longer matters. Only one doubt is left (before or after אירוסין), and a single doubt does not get the ספק ספיקא leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not needed' except for this case: the ruling is about a specific situation
The wife of a כהן

phrases.english: No, it is needed for the wife of a kohen.
phrases.notes: A כהן's wife is forbidden to him even if she was forced, so the second doubt drops away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ספק ספיקא challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to apply to any wife, where there are two doubts.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies to an אשת כהן, where אונס also forbids, leaving only one doubt.

steps.title: Second answer: a girl betrothed before age three
steps.stepSummary: The ruling can apply even to an אשת ישראל if her father betrothed her before she was three years and a day old, removing the 'before or after' doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say it is about the wife of a ישראל, in a case where her father accepted קידושין for her when she was younger than three years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that removes the OTHER doubt, the question of before or after the אירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before age three and a day, the signs of בתולים grow back after relations. So if she was betrothed that young, anything that happened before the קידושין left no mark. What the husband found must have happened after. Only the 'forced or willing' doubt remains, which is a single doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': introduces another answer
The wife of a regular Jew (not a כהן)
Accepted betrothal (on her behalf)
Three years and one day old

steps.whatToRemember: The two answers each knock out a different doubt: אשת כהן removes 'forced or willing'; betrothal under three removes 'before or after'.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: with the wife of a Yisrael,
in a case where her father accepted betrothal for her

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: when she was less than three years and one day old.
phrases.notes: Before this age the signs of בתולים grow back, so what he found must have happened after the קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With an אשת ישראל there seem to be two doubts.
steps.terutzMaskana: If betrothed under age three, the 'before or after' doubt is gone, leaving one doubt.

steps.title: What does the ruling add? A משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: If only one doubt remains, the ruling seems obvious: a משנה already shows a person can forbid something to himself by his own claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us? We already learned: if a man says to a woman 'I betrothed you,' and she says 'You did not betroth me,' she may marry his relatives, and he may not marry her relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the ruling from a new angle: it seems unnecessary, because an existing משנה already teaches the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the man's own word that she is betrothed to him forbids him to her relatives, even with no witnesses. That already shows a person is believed to forbid things to himself. So why would we need the ruling about פתח פתוח?

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does it teach us?': the ruling seems to add nothing new
'I betrothed you'
His relatives / her relatives

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the ruling's correctness. The גמרא agrees with it and only asks why it needed to be said at all.

phrases.english: What does it teach us? We already learned:
One who says to a woman: 'I betrothed you,'
and she says: 'You did not betroth me'
she is permitted to his relatives,
and he is forbidden to her relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 3 and 4 reduce the case to one doubt, this asks why the ruling is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ruling of step 1, once it is a case of a single doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already shows that a person's own claim forbids things to himself, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Why the ruling is not obvious after all
steps.stepSummary: The ruling needed to be taught. In the משנה's case the man surely knows the facts, but here the husband might not truly know whether she was a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, he knows for certain. But here, maybe he does not really know. So the ruling teaches us that he is still believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5 by showing why רבי אלעזר's ruling adds something new beyond the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, the man knows for sure whether he did the קידושין. A husband claiming פתח פתוח could easily be mistaken, so we might have thought his claim is too weak to forbid her. רבי אלעזר teaches that even this less-certain claim is believed to forbid her to him.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introducing a mistaken assumption)
It is clear to him; he knows for sure
It may well be (introducing a real possibility)
It teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: You might have said:
there, where he certainly knows clearly,
phrases.notes: "There" is the משנה from step 5, where a man tells a woman that he did קידושין with her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא מֵיקָם הוּא דְּלָא קִים לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: but here, it may well be that he does not know clearly,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (certain knowledge vs. possible mistake)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A husband's claim of פתח פתוח is not reliable enough to forbid her, since he may be mistaken
steps.terutzMaskana: Even so, his claim is believed to forbid her to himself

steps.title: Contradiction from another statement of רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר also said that a wife becomes forbidden to her husband only through קינוי וסתירה, based on the incident of דוד and בת שבע. How then can a claim of פתח פתוח forbid her?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי אלעזר really say this? But he said: a woman becomes forbidden to her husband only through warning and seclusion, like the incident that happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling by quoting a different statement of his that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second statement limits how a wife becomes forbidden to her husband: only when he warned her (קינוי) and she then secluded herself with that man (סתירה). A husband's private claim of פתח פתוח is not on that list. So the two statements of רבי אלעזר seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? (opens a contradiction)
A husband's formal warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man
Seclusion; the wife being alone with that man after the warning
The incident that happened (דוד and בת שבע)

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Elazar really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
A woman does not become forbidden to her husband
except through matters of warning and seclusion,
and like the incident that happened!
phrases.notes: This means the story of דוד and בת שבע.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the ruling just defended
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a husband is believed to forbid his wife by claiming פתח פתוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two statements of the same אמורא: only קינוי וסתירה forbids a wife, so a claim of פתח פתוח should not

steps.title: The quoted statement does not fit the story itself
steps.stepSummary: Before dealing with the contradiction, the גמרא points out that the quote does not make sense as worded. The incident of דוד and בת שבע had no קינוי וסתירה, and בת שבע was never forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that? Did the incident that happened involve warning and seclusion? And besides, was she made forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the wording of the quoted statement, because the story it refers to does not match it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote says "like the incident that happened," as if that story was a case of קינוי וסתירה that made a wife forbidden. But that story had no warning and no seclusion. Also, בת שבע was not treated as forbidden. So the quote must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (questions an assumption)
And furthermore
They made her forbidden

phrases.english: And can you really think so?
The incident that happened — was it with warning and seclusion?
And furthermore, did they make her forbidden?
phrases.notes: "Her" is בת שבע, who was not treated as forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה, בְּקִינּוּי וּסְתִירָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the source quoted in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "וּכְמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה" in רבי אלעזר's second statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story it cites had neither קינוי וסתירה nor a resulting prohibition, so it cannot be an example of the rule

steps.title: Reading the story as the source for the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the quote. The story is not an example of קינוי וסתירה. It is the proof: since there was no קינוי וסתירה, she was not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. This is what he means: a woman becomes forbidden to her husband only through warning and seclusion. We learn this from the incident that happened, where there was no warning and seclusion, and she did not become forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording problem from step 8 by explaining what רבי אלעזר really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Like the incident" is read as "from the incident." Because the story had no קינוי וסתירה, בת שבע was not forbidden. That shows only קינוי וסתירה forbids a wife. This solves the wording issue but leaves the clash with the פתח פתוח ruling untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult
This is what he means (rereading a statement)
She became forbidden

phrases.english: That is not difficult;
this is what he is saying:
A woman does not become forbidden to her husband
except through matters of warning and seclusion,
as we learn from the incident that happened,
where there was no warning and seclusion
and so she did not become forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement ("like the incident" becomes "from the incident")
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story was quoted as an example of קינוי וסתירה causing a prohibition
steps.terutzMaskana: The story is the source: with no קינוי וסתירה, there was no prohibition

steps.title: The contradiction still stands
steps.stepSummary: Even with the corrected reading, רבי אלעזר still says only קינוי וסתירה forbids a wife. That implies a claim of פתח פתוח does not, which contradicts his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult: warning and seclusion, yes; "an open opening," no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main contradiction from step 7 and shows it is still unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixing the wording did not change the rule itself. The rule is that only קינוי וסתירה forbids a wife to her husband. A husband's claim of פתח פתוח is not קינוי וסתירה, so it should not forbid her. That still clashes with רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it is still difficult
An open opening (the husband's claim that she was not a בתולה)
Yes / no (contrasting two cases)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 9's "הא לא קשיא" only fixed the side problem about the story's wording. It did not answer the main contradiction, and that is why the גמרא now says "מכל מקום קשיא."

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult:
warning and seclusion — yes, she becomes forbidden;
"an open opening" — no!
phrases.notes: This is the husband's claim from step 1, that he found his bride was not a בתולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main contradiction of step 7 after the wording issue was resolved
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a claim of פתח פתוח forbids the wife to her husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from 'only קינוי וסתירה': any other cause, including a claim of פתח פתוח, does not forbid her

steps.title: Witnesses obviously forbid a wife too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the inference from step 10. If רבי אלעזר meant that only קינוי וסתירה forbids a wife, then two witnesses would not forbid her, and that cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, קינוי וסתירה forbids her, but witnesses do not?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the inference from step 10 proves too much. Reading רבי אלעזר as 'only קינוי וסתירה forbids' would mean witnesses don't forbid her, which is clearly false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 read רבי אלעזר's words as a strict limit: nothing except קינוי וסתירה forbids a wife. The גמרא points out that this strict reading would also rule out two witnesses who saw her sin. Everyone agrees witnesses forbid her, so the strict reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: used to show that the other side's logic leads to an impossible result
Yes
Witnesses

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:
warning and seclusion, yes, forbid her,
but witnesses do not?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the strict inference that step 10 drew from רבי אלעזר's words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that only קינוי וסתירה can forbid a wife.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would wrongly exclude two witnesses, who certainly forbid her.

steps.title: Rereading רבי אלעזר: one witness, two witnesses, and פתח פתוח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר really means that one witness does not forbid a wife, only two witnesses do. After קינוי וסתירה even one witness is enough, and a claim of פתח פתוח counts like two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: a woman is not forbidden to her husband by one witness, only by two witnesses. With קינוי וסתירה, even one witness is enough. And פתח פתוח is treated like two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of רבי אלעזר's statement. This solves the contradiction with his ruling on פתח פתוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement was never about which events forbid her. It is about how much evidence is needed: normally two witnesses, but after קינוי וסתירה one witness is enough. The husband's claim of פתח פתוח counts like two witnesses, so it can forbid her even without קינוי וסתירה.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness
Two witnesses, the normal full proof
The husband warns his wife not to be alone with a certain man, and she is then alone with him
'An open opening': the husband's claim that he found his new wife was not a בתולה
Is like, is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר is talking about how much evidence is needed. Two witnesses forbid a wife. After קינוי וסתירה one witness is enough. A claim of פתח פתוח counts like two witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the contradiction from step 10, so רבי אלעזר's ruling that a claim of פתח פתוח forbids the wife still stands.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:
A woman is not forbidden to her husband
through one witness, only through two witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: וְקִינּוּי וּסְתִירָה — אֲפִילּוּ בְּעֵד אֶחָד נָמֵי.
phrases.english: And where there was warning and seclusion, even through one witness as well.
And an open opening is like two witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 knocks down the strict reading, this gives the correct reading and resolves step 10's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement: it is about how much evidence is needed, not a list of what forbids a wife.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר meant that only קינוי וסתירה can forbid a wife, which would clash with his ruling on פתח פתוח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two witnesses forbid her, after קינוי וסתירה one witness is enough, and פתח פתוח counts like two witnesses.

steps.title: Why was בת שבע not forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the statement no longer explains the story of דוד and בת שבע through קינוי וסתירה, the גמרא asks why בת שבע was not forbidden to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: in the incident that happened, why did they not forbid her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the story of דוד and בת שבע. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, the lack of קינוי וסתירה no longer explains why בת שבע stayed permitted. Since it was known that דוד had been with her, why was she not forbidden to her husband?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a question the listener might ask
The incident that happened, here the story of דוד and בת שבע
They forbade her

phrases.english: And if you will say: the incident that happened,
phrases.notes: This is the story of דוד and בת שבע mentioned in step 7.

phrases.english: why did they not forbid her?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why was she not forbidden to her husband אוריה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reading in step 12 no longer explains the story through קינוי וסתירה, so the story itself now needs an explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that בת שבע was not forbidden to her husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דוד was with a married woman, so she should have become forbidden, yet she was not.

steps.title: First answer: it was אונס
steps.stepSummary: בת שבע was not forbidden because it was אונס. She did not take part willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: בת שבע was not willing, so she stayed permitted to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife of a ישראל (not a כהן) becomes forbidden to her husband only if she was willing. Since בת שבע was taken by force, she was not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case
Being forced, not by her own choice

phrases.english: There it was by force.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a detail of the case: it was אונס, so she was not forbidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since דוד was with her, she should have been forbidden to her husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was forced, and a wife who is forced stays permitted to her husband.

steps.title: Second answer begins: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a second answer for why בת שבע was not forbidden, based on a teaching of רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן. The teaching itself comes in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: like that which רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second answer. It introduces a teaching of רבי שמואל בר נחמני, which is quoted right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואיבעית אימא' means the גמרא is offering a different answer to the same question. Here we only get who said it; what he said comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another answer

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: like that which רבי שמואל בר נחמני said
that רבי יונתן said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 13, alongside the אונס answer of step 14.
